title: Realization of the native Weil evaluation transpose
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X$ put $\bar X=X\times_{k_0}k$ and let $g_{\bar X}$ be geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. On the small pro-etale site of $\bar X$, let $R_{\bar X}$ be the coefficient sheaf whose sections on a quasi-compact object $V$ are continuous functions $|V|\to\Omega$ with values in one finite intermediate extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$; on general objects impose this condition locally [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. Write $\mathcal A_{\bar X}=\operatorname{Mod}(R_{\bar X})$ for its module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $\mathcal B_{\bar X}$ for pairs $(F,\theta:g_{\bar X}^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}F)$ in $\mathcal A_{\bar X}$, with intertwining morphisms [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Derived categories mean localization of complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathrm{WC}(X)\subset D(\mathcal B_{\bar X})$ be the full subcategory with bounded cohomology whose underlying cohomology sheaves admit a finite locally closed stratification with pro-etale locally finite free restrictions over $R_{\bar X}$. This is the native category `AlgebraicGeometry.WeilComplex`, not the category of fixed pairs in $D(\mathcal A_{\bar X})$.

Let $a_0:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ be the structure morphism and let $Ra_{0!}^{\mathrm W}:\mathrm{WC}(X)\to\mathrm{WC}(\operatorname{Spec}k_0)$ be the native compact-support functor `AlgebraicGeometry.WeilComplex.derivedLowerShriek`, formed from equivariant open extension by zero and proper direct image along a compactification [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Assume that $Ra_{0!}^{\mathrm W}$ has a right adjoint $Ra_0^{!,\mathrm W}$ on $\mathrm{WC}$, as in `WeilComplex.HasUpperShriek`. Put $\omega_X=Ra_0^{!,\mathrm W}\Omega^{\mathrm W}$, where $\Omega^{\mathrm W}$ is $R_s[0]$ with its canonical Frobenius pullback isomorphism at $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. For $K,L\in D(\mathcal B_{\bar X})$ let $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal B_{\bar X}}(K,L)$ be the native derived internal Hom `ProEtaleWeilSheaf.derivedHom`: choose a K-injective resolution $L\to I$ in complexes over $\mathcal B_{\bar X}$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex] and take the product total complex $\prod_p\mathcal Hom_{R_{\bar X}}(K^p,I^{p+n})$ of internal Hom sheaves of $R_{\bar X}$-modules, each with the contragredient Weil structure $\theta_I\circ(-)\circ\theta_K^{-1}$ (through the canonical isomorphism $g^*\mathcal Hom(A,B)\cong\mathcal Hom(g^*A,g^*B)$ for the automorphism $g=g_{\bar X}$). 

Put $Y=\bar X$, $\mathcal C_Y=D^b_c(Y,\Omega)$, the common finite-coefficient-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], with raw rationalizations [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and $\omega_Y=Ra_Y^!\Omega$ for $a_Y:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, using the constructible exceptional functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write $D_YM=R\mathcal Hom(M,\omega_Y)$ for the coefficient-passage internal Hom [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; by [thm-coef-qbar-verdier] it is an anti-equivalence of $\mathcal C_Y$, so $D_YM$ and $D_YD_YM$ lie in $\mathcal C_Y$ for $M\in\mathcal C_Y$. Let $\rho_Y:\mathcal C_Y\simeq D^b_{\mathrm{cons}}(\mathcal A_Y)$ be the evaluation-normalized coefficient realization [lem-sf-adic-qbar-constructible-realization], and $U:D(\mathcal B_Y)\to D(\mathcal A_Y)$ the termwise forgetful functor [lem-sf-weil-native-closed-forgetful]. Here $D^b_{\mathrm{cons}}$ means bounded cohomology whose sheaves have a finite locally closed stratification with pro-etale locally finite free restrictions over $R_Y$. Fix an inverse equivalence to $\rho_Y$, including its unit and counit. For $K\in\mathrm{WC}(X)$ set $M_K=\rho_Y^{-1}UK$ and denote its counit isomorphism by $j_K:\rho_YM_K\xrightarrow{\sim}UK$. Write $H_XK=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal B_Y}(K,\omega_X)$ in the ambient native derived category.

Let $h:U\omega_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_Y\omega_Y$ be the counit-normalized isomorphism for the specified exceptional adjoint [lem-sf-weil-native-exceptional-forgetful]. For each $K$ define $c_K:UH_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_YD_YM_K$ as the composite of the forgetful Hom comparison, the Hom map induced by $j_K$ and $h$, and the inverse evaluation-transpose realization comparison. Assume that $H_X$ takes $\mathrm{WC}(X)$ to itself; write $D_X$ for this restriction. No invertibility of a native double-dual map is assumed.

There is a natural transformation $\delta^X:\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{WC}(X)}\to D_XD_X$, whose component is the ambient tensor--Hom transpose characterized by
$$\operatorname{ev}_{D_XK,\omega_X}\circ(\delta^X_K\otimes1_{D_XK})=\operatorname{ev}_{K,\omega_X}\circ\sigma_{K,D_XK}.$$
Here $\sigma$ is the derived tensor symmetry. Put $\delta^Y_M:M\to D_YD_YM$ for the same transpose in the common-stage category. Define
$$b_K:UD_XD_XK\xrightarrow{c_{D_XK}}\rho_YD_YM_{D_XK}\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_YD_YD_YM_K,$$
where the second isomorphism is obtained by applying $\rho_YD_Y$ contravariantly to the inverse of $\rho_Y^{-1}c_K$, using the fixed inverse-equivalence unit identifications. Then
$$b_K\circ U(\delta^X_K)\circ j_K=\rho_Y(\delta^Y_{M_K}).$$
This is an equality of morphisms in $D(\mathcal A_Y)$, natural in every native derived morphism; it concerns the specified evaluation transpose, including the symmetry in its definition. No isomorphism assertion for $\delta^X$ is part of this statement.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-weil-native-closed-forgetful] with $T_0=X$ and $W=\omega_X$. Its symmetric closed structure is on the actual ambient $D(\mathcal B_Y)$ and its Hom is the specified native Hom. It supplies a natural morphism $\delta^W_K:K\to H_XH_XK$ as the transpose of $\operatorname{ev}_{K,\omega_X}\circ\sigma_{K,H_XK}$, with precisely the equation in the statement. By the assumed closure of $H_X$ on $\mathrm{WC}(X)$, both $H_XK$ and $H_XH_XK$ belong to that full subcategory. Restrict the components and their naturality equations to it, defining $\delta^X:\mathrm{id}\to D_XD_X$. Write $u_K=U(\delta^X_K)$ and $e^U_K:UD_XK\otimes UK\to U\omega_X$ for the image of native evaluation under the specified tensor comparison. Preservation of symmetry gives $e^U_{D_XK}\circ(u_K\otimes1)=e^U_K\circ\sigma_{UK,UD_XK}$.

source.place: Paragraph beginning “The first map”: evaluation and transposition, in the native derived model.

proof.text: Write $\rho=\rho_Y$, $D=D_Y$, and $M=M_K$. By [thm-coef-qbar-verdier], $M,DM,DDM$ are in $\mathcal C_Y$ and the common-stage $\delta^Y_M$ is the evaluation transpose. Let $\mu_{A,B}:\rho A\otimes\rho B\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho(A\otimes B)$ be the realization tensorator and put $E_A=\rho(\operatorname{ev}_{A,\omega_Y})\circ\mu_{DA,A}$. All tensors below are derived. The evaluation-transpose comparison of [lem-sf-adic-qbar-constructible-realization] identifies $\rho DDM$ with the ambient internal Hom from $\rho DM$ to $\rho\omega_Y$. Thus the adjunction of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] makes $z\mapsto E_{DM}\circ(z\otimes1_{\rho DM})$ injective on arrows $\rho M\to\rho DDM$. The defining transpose equation and preservation of symmetry also give $E_{DM}\circ(\rho(\delta^Y_M)\otimes1)=E_M\circ\sigma_{\rho M,\rho DM}$.

proof.text:
Use the explicit comparison in [def-sf-weil-dual-realization-comparison-data] for $K$ and $D_XK$, allowed by assumed closure. Its $c$ is exactly the composite specified here with the same counit-normalized $h$. Set $N=M_{D_XK}$. Full faithfulness of the realization equivalence defines an isomorphism $t:N\xrightarrow{\sim}DM$ by $\rho(t)=c_K\circ j_{D_XK}$. The fixed inverse-equivalence unit identifies $t$ with $\rho^{-1}c_K$ in the question, so $b_K=\rho D(t^{-1})\circ c_{D_XK}$ and $\rho(t^{-1})=j_{D_XK}^{-1}\circ c_K^{-1}$. The cited comparison's evaluation clause gives
$$E_M\circ(c_K\otimes1_{\rho M})=h\circ e^U_K\circ(1\otimes j_K),\qquad E_N\circ(c_{D_XK}\otimes1_{\rho N})=h\circ e^U_{D_XK}\circ(1\otimes j_{D_XK}).$$
These are equations of the actual arrows in the ambient module derived category, with the specified $h$. In Lean, derive both evaluation squares directly by uncurrying sectionHomComparison and applying HomLaws.evaluation; derive comparison naturality from sectionHomComparison, HomLaws.naturality and counit naturality. This avoids importing the older dual-realization comparison interface.

source.place: Last paragraph: comparisons built from scalar tensor, dualizing counit and evaluation; fixed inverse-equivalence unit and counit.

proof.text:
Use the naturality in the first Hom argument of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] for the ambient arrow $\rho(t^{-1}):\rho DM\to\rho N$ and target $\rho\omega_Y$. The Hom comparisons of [lem-sf-adic-qbar-constructible-realization] identify the two ambient Hom objects with $\rho DDM$ and $\rho DN$; these comparisons are natural in both variables and carry evaluation to evaluation. The counit formula for the cited adjunction therefore gives
$$E_{DM}\circ(\rho D(t^{-1})\otimes1_{\rho DM})=E_N\circ(1_{\rho DN}\otimes\rho(t^{-1})).$$
Indeed, both sides are the uncurrying of the ambient Hom precomposition map composed with the comparison from $\rho DN$. This is one substitution in ambient adjunction naturality; all the Hom objects are constructible by step 2 applied to $M$ and $N$.

source.place: Transposition paragraph: naturality of evaluation under the inverse first-dual identification.

proof.text:
Put $z=b_K\circ u_K\circ j_K$. Substitute $b_K$ and step 4, then the second equation of step 3 and $j_{D_XK}\circ\rho(t^{-1})=c_K^{-1}$:
$$\begin{aligned}
E_{DM}\circ(z\otimes1)
&=E_N\circ(c_{D_XK}u_Kj_K\otimes\rho(t^{-1}))\\
&=h\circ e^U_{D_XK}\circ(u_Kj_K\otimes c_K^{-1})\\
&=h\circ e^U_K\circ\sigma_{UK,UD_XK}\circ(j_K\otimes c_K^{-1})\\
&=h\circ e^U_K\circ(c_K^{-1}\otimes j_K)\circ\sigma_{\rho M,\rho DM}\\
&=E_M\circ\sigma_{\rho M,\rho DM}.
\end{aligned}$$
The third line is the native transpose equation of [lem-sf-weil-native-closed-forgetful]; the fourth is naturality of the signed symmetry preserved by realization; the last is the first equation of the explicit comparison in [def-sf-weil-dual-realization-comparison-data] precomposed with $c_K^{-1}\otimes1$. Tensor functoriality and associativity justify each regrouping. This computes the pairing explicitly without cancellation of $U$ on morphisms.

source.place: “Naturality of evaluation proves its equivariance, and transposition gives the same conclusion for δ”: explicit two-evaluation calculation including symmetry.

proof.text: The last pairing in step 5 also belongs to $\rho(\delta^Y_M)$ by step 2. Injectivity of the ambient transpose bijection therefore gives $b_K\circ U(\delta^X_K)\circ j_K=\rho(\delta^Y_{M_K})$. This holds naturally for every native derived morphism: $\delta^X$ is natural by step 1, $j$ is the inverse-equivalence counit, and $c$ is natural even on extension morphisms by the explicit comparison in [def-sf-weil-dual-realization-comparison-data]. For $f:K\to L$ put $M_f=\rho^{-1}Uf$; those naturality equations give $t_K\circ M_{D_Xf}=D(M_f)\circ t_L$. Apply the contravariant $D$ to the inverse-isomorphism rearrangement to obtain the naturality of $\rho D(t^{-1})$, hence of $b$. All comparison equations are natural, so these component equalities give the asserted natural equality. Only the isomorphisms $c,j,t,h$ were inverted; no invertibility of $\delta^X$ was used or claimed.
